page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under a KVM hypervisor, this instance provides 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, running at a clock speed of 3.2 GHz. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities for standard compute tasks, though raw CPU execution speeds fall into lower percentiles. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng benchmarks are positioned in the bottom 25 percent, as are the Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in specific workloads, such as software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and text processing. Memory read bandwidth is average at 414.69 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 39.89 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, while large block write bandwidth is weaker at 23.56 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced memory-to-core ratio, the ecs.cm4.2xlarge is suited for moderate general-purpose workloads. It performs adequately for static web serving, Redis operations, and light text or image processing. However, it is less efficient for resource-intensive database operations or modern LLM inference, where it registers poor performance on 7B models. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile offers a stable, dedicated resource allocation for legacy x86_64 applications that do not require high-speed local NVMe storage or advanced AVX-512 vector instructions.
